arxiv-2012-12031.title: Towards Quantifying Privacy in Process Mining
arxiv-2012-12031.creator: Majid Rafiei, Wil M.P. van der Aalst
arxiv-2012-12031.description: Abstract Process mining employs event logs to provide insights into the actual processes. Event logs are recorded by information systems and contain valuable information helping organizations to improve their processes. However, these data also include highly sensitive private information which is a major concern when applying process mining.

arxiv-2202-05669.title: Novel Approaches to Solve Simple Harmonic Motion
arxiv-2202-05669.creator: Zhiwei Chong
arxiv-2202-05669.description: Abstract This paper presents two novel approaches to solve the classic simple harmonic motion. In one approach, the distance between the equilibrium position and the maximal displacement is divided into N N equal segments. In each segment, the mass moves with constant acceleration under the average of two forces at the ends of the segment.

arxiv-2202-06325.title: Single-cell Bayesian deconvolution
arxiv-2202-06325.creator: Gabriel Torregrosa, David Oriola, Vikas Trivedi, Jordi Garcia-Ojalvo
arxiv-2202-06325.description: Abstract Individual cells exhibit substantial heterogeneity in protein abundance and activity, which is frequently reflected in broad distributions of fluorescently labeled reporters. Since all cellular components are intrinsically fluorescent to some extent, the observed distributions contain background noise that masks the natural heterogeneity of cellular populations.

arxiv-2211-09328.creator: Oriol Solé Pi

arxiv-2302-03859.title: In-orbit performance of HE onboard Insight -HXMT in the first 5 years
arxiv-2302-03859.creator: Xu-Fang Li, Cong-Zhan Liu, Yi-Fei Zhang, Xiao-Bo Li, Zheng-Wei Li, Xue-Feng Lu, Zhi Chang, Ming-Yu Ge, Juan Zhang, Yu-Peng Xu, Fang-Jun Lu, Li-Ming Song, Shuang-Nan Zhang

arxiv-2302-14727.title: Automatically Classifying Emotions based on Text: A Comparative Exploration of Different Datasets
arxiv-2302-14727.creator: Anna Koufakou, Jairo Garciga, Adam Paul, Joseph Morelli and Christopher Frank
arxiv-2302-14727.description: Abstract Emotion Classification based on text is a task with many applications which has received growing interest in recent years. This paper presents a preliminary study with the goal to help researchers and practitioners gain insight into relatively new datasets as well as emotion classification in general.

arxiv-2305-16036.title: The Weak Galerkin Finite Element Method For The Steklov Eigenvalue Problem
arxiv-2305-16036.creator: Shusheng Li, Hehu Xie, Qilong Zhai
arxiv-2305-16036.description: Abstract This paper introduces a weak Galerkin (WG) finite element method to solve the Steklov eigenvalue problems, focusing on obtaining lower bounds of the eigenvalues. Compared with the existing work, our method can provide asymptotic lower bound approximations of eigenvalues with arbitrary high order convergence and no additional conditions are required.

arxiv-2308-09684.title: Algebraic string topology from the neighborhood of infinity
arxiv-2308-09684.creator: Manuel Rivera, Alex Takeda and Zhengfang Wang
arxiv-2308-09684.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Manuel Rivera, Alex Takeda and Zhengfang Wang. We construct and study an algebraic analogue of the loop coproduct in string topology, also known as the Goresky-Hingston coproduct. Our algebraic setup, which under this analogy takes the place of the complex of chains on the free loop space of a possibly non-simply connected oriented manifold, is the Hochschild chain complex of a smooth A ∞ A_{\infty} -category equipped with a pre-Calabi-Yau structure and a trivialization of a version of the Chern character of its diagonal

arxiv-2401-09299.title: Scaled quadratic variation for controlled rough paths and parameter estimation of fractional diffusions
arxiv-2401-09299.creator: James-Michael Leahy 1, Torstein Nilssen 2
arxiv-2401-09299.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by James-Michael Leahy 1, Torstein Nilssen 2. We introduce the concept of finite γ \gamma -scaled quadratic variation along a sequence of partitions for paths on a given interval. This concept, with historical roots in the study of Gaussian processes by Gladyshev (1961) and Klein & Giné (1975), includes the fractional Brownian motion (fBm) with Hurst index H H , which has finite 1 − 2 ​ H 1-2H -scaled quadratic variation.

arxiv-2411-09933.title: JRadiEvo: A Japanese Radiology Report Generation Model Enhanced by Evolutionary Optimization of Model Merging
arxiv-2411-09933.creator: Kaito Baba, Ryota Yagi, Junichiro Takahashi, Risa Kishikawa, Satoshi Kodera
arxiv-2411-09933.description: Abstract With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs), foundational models (FMs) have seen significant advancements. Healthcare is one of the most crucial application areas for these FMs, given the significant time and effort required for physicians to analyze large volumes of patient data.

arxiv-2502-07541.title: Detecting Greenwashing: A Natural Language Processing Literature Survey
arxiv-2502-07541.creator: Tom Calamai, Oana Balalau, Théo Le Guenedal, Fabian Suchanek
arxiv-2502-07541.description: Abstract Greenwashing refers to practices by corporations or governments that intentionally mislead the public about their environmental impact. This paper provides a comprehensive and methodologically grounded survey of natural language processing (NLP) approaches for detecting greenwashing in textual data, with a focus on corporate climate communication.

arxiv-2510-18496.title: LatticeHashForest: An Efficient Data Structure for Repetitive Data and Operations
arxiv-2510-18496.creator: Anamitra Ghorui, Uday P. Khedker
arxiv-2510-18496.description: Abstract The domain of program analysis and optimization forms a very fundamental part of compilers and software toolchains. Analysis of entire programs as a single unit, or whole-program analysis, involves propagation of large amounts of information through the control flow of the program.

arxiv-2601-21178.title: U ​ ( 1 ) A U(1)_{A} symmetry restoration at finite temperature with mesonic correlators
arxiv-2601-21178.creator: Antonio Smecca
arxiv-2601-21178.description: Abstract The U ​ ( 1 ) A U(1)_{A} symmetry of the massless QCD Lagrangian is explicitly broken in the quantised theory by the anomaly. It may be effectively restored at some finite temperature, which would have important consequences for the order of the chiral transition and the QCD phase diagram.

plos-pone-0001247.title: Brain Responses to Violet, Blue, and Green Monochromatic Light Exposures in Humans: Prominent Role of Blue Light and the Brainstem
plos-pone-0001247.creator: Gilles Vandewalle, Christina Schmidt, Geneviève Albouy et al.
plos-pone-0001247.description: PLOS ONE research article. Relatively long duration retinal light exposure elicits nonvisual responses in humans, including modulation of alertness and cognition. These responses are thought to be mediated in part by melanopsin-expressing retinal ganglion cells which are more sensitive to blue light than v

pmc-11413036.title: E148Q variant: a familial Mediterranean fever-causing mutation or a sequence variant?
pmc-11413036.creator: Elham Orouk Awaad, Lana Khoury, Joeri W. van Straalen, Adi Miller-Barmak, Tal Gazitt, Jumana Haddad-Haloun, Riva Brik, Mohamad Hamad Saied
pmc-11413036.description: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an autosomal recessive autoinflammatory disease, linked to mutations in the MEFV gene. The p.E148Q variant, found on exon 2, has an uncertain role in FMF, with debates on whether it is a benign polymorphism or a pathogenic mutation.

pmc-12471145.title: Expanding Applications of Three-Dimensional Cardiac Mapping Systems: A Review
pmc-12471145.creator: Rabeia Javid, Stephen O Otieno, Stephen B Wheatcroft, Sacchin Arockiam, Muzahir H Tayebjee, Attila Nemes, Roberto De Ponti
pmc-12471145.description: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a widely performed revascularisation procedure for coronary artery disease. Although effective, its reliance on fluoroscopy and iodinated contrast exposes patients and operators to risks of radiation and nephrotoxicity. As PCI techniques have become more complex, interest has grown in imaging methods that reduce dependence on fluoroscopy and contrast.

pmc-12829265.title: Explainable AI models for identifying anxiety and distress in cardiac patients with ICDs
pmc-12829265.creator: Ali Ebrahimi, Jakob Bo Reinevald Eriksen, David Krogh Kølbæk, Jonas Mohr Pedersen, Ebbe Vincent Just Christensen, Søren Skovbakke, Ole Skov, Susanne Schmidt Pedersen, Amir Sorayaie Azar, Uffe Kock Wiil
pmc-12829265.description: BackgroundCardiac patients with Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators (ICDs) are at elevated risk of experiencing anxiety, depression, or general psychological distress. Nevertheless, routine psychological screening in cardiology care is limited, and early identification of vulnerable individuals remains a challenge, particularly in settings transitioning to remote monitoring. Scalable, data-driven tools are urgently needed to support timely detection and intervention.

pmc-12847764.title: Blue enriched light modulates pupil dilation induced by transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation
pmc-12847764.creator: Inci Cakiroglu, Enrique Germany Morrison, Sarah Brisbois, Venethia Danthine, Ana Marta Dias, Antoine Nonclercq, Gilles Vandewalle, Riëm El Tahry
pmc-12847764.description: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) targets the auricular branch of the vagus nerve and can modulate brainstem arousal systems, including the locus coeruleus–noradrenaline (LC-NE) pathway. Blue-enriched light also affects LC activity and can enhance alertness and cognition. However, no study has tested whether combining tVNS with blue light could further boost noradrenergic activity in humans.

pmc-13028982.title: Editorial for “Gut Microbiota, Diet, and Gastrointestinal Cancer”
pmc-13028982.creator: Marco Cintoni, Flavio De Maio
pmc-13028982.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The bidirectional relationship between the host and its microbial communities influences not only local carcinogenic processes—through inflammation, immune dysregulation, and microbial metabolite production—but also systemic immune responses and the effectiveness of anticancer therapies [3]. In this Special Issue, “Gut Microbiota, Diet, and Gastrointestinal Cancer,” we compile nine articles, ranging from original research and pilot studies to comprehensive reviews, that collectively enhance our knowledge of how the microbiome serves as a diagnostic biomarker, a mechanistic driver of disease, and a promising therapeutic target.

pmc-13079801.title: Ternary solvation sheath reconfiguration drives sustainable cryogenic Li||Cl2 batteries
pmc-13079801.creator: Qihao Liu, Guanzhong Ma, Ling Wei, Caili Zhang, Jiajun Geng, Junwei Han, Debin Kong, Linjie Zhi
pmc-13079801.description: Rechargeable Li | |Cl2 batteries hold promise for low temperature storage but suffer from interfacial instability due to electrolyte decomposition, particularly at cryogenic temperatures. We identify the failure mechanism as a complex solvation chemistry involving Li+, reactive SOCl2, and coordinating chloroaluminates that drives parasitic reactions.

pmc-13088438.title: RGReco: a unified framework for automated R-group recognition in chemical publications
pmc-13088438.creator: Yuanjie Xiang, Yanghong Luo, Renshuang Liu, Jiajun Tao, Wei Hu, Mei Ouyang, Wei Liu
pmc-13088438.description: The abundant R-group information available in chemical publications plays a crucial role in data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) research in the field of medicinal chemistry. In real-world publications, R-groups are expressed in various textual and graphical forms, thereby rendering their manual integration labor-intensive and inefficient.

pmc-13294161.title: When Complex Models Fit the Wrong Mechanistic Complexity in Phylogenomic Analysis
pmc-13294161.creator: Liang Liu, David A Liberles
pmc-13294161.description: Substitution model selection is central to phylogenetic inference and is commonly treated as a problem of identifying the substitutional complexity required to describe sequence evolution along a single tree. This framework implicitly assumes a shared genealogy across all sites, an assumption that is routinely violated in phylogenomic data by incomplete lineage sorting and other sources of gene-tree discordance.
